claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events measures 14.39 km against a booked optimal of 12.0 km, an excess of 2.39 km. That excess is 19.92% of optimal, which clears the 20% limb of the establishment test only if the trace figure governs — and POL-RD-01 says the trace figure governs, expressly forbidding reliance on the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 14.4 km. The absolute limb is also met: 2.39 km is greater than the 0.8 km threshold. Both tests pass, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The driver's only explanation is a bare assertion in his counterparty statement — 'Minor detour because of a road works sign.' He names no advisory, no road and no evidence ID. Under POL-RD-08 the burden shifted to him once the rider showed the excess, and a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge it. The assertion is discarded and carries no weight.

Even if the driver's road-works excuse were treated as an invocation of POL-RD-03, it cannot be run: the bundle's only traffic advisory artifact is MISSING, weight 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and the note that no advisory covers the Jurong Point corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window overlapping the trace; with no advisory on file that comparison cannot be made, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight. The absence is itself citable, and it is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 113 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs fires. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone at the measured figure, and the driver's traffic assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal route.

No exculpatory clause on the driver's side is available on this record. There is no chat_log at all — 0 messages — so POL-RD-04's rider-requested-detour exoneration cannot be invoked and its corroboration test cannot even be run. The trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, so POL-RD-05's relocation re-quote does not apply. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. Nothing excuses the excess.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the booked optimal route because no adjustment clause applies. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 16.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = (3.80 + 9.00 + 4.48) + 0.80 = 18.08. Refund = charged_total 20.64 less 18.08 = 2.56, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.60 once rounded up to the nearest 0.05.

The fare ledger carries no ERP or toll lines at all — erp_gantries is empty and the off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00 — and no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through correction to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's recovery is the distance-and-time refund and nothing more.

The deviation is not MATERIAL: the excess of 2.39 km is well under the 8.0 km absolute materiality threshold and 19.92% is under the 50% materiality threshold, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows from this trip. I do not claim a repeat-deviation pattern, and I note the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 in any event.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim: deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift for a serial claimant is not engaged and the trace alone carries the excess. The rider's other profile fields — rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes — are context only under POL-GEN-01 and I cite none of them as a ground of decision.

claims.text: The rider's own claim is that the trip ran 14.39 km against a 12.0 km optimal route. The governing trace figure is 14.39 km (EV-GPS-02817), and the platform's own derived deviation block computes an excess of 2.39 km, which is 19.92% of the 12.0 km optimal. That excess is below the 20% establishment threshold set by POL-RD-01, so no deviation is established and the rider's claim fails on the threshold test itself.

POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute. The trace excess of 2.39 km clears the 0.8 km absolute limb, but the 19.92% figure does not clear the 20% proportional limb. Because both tests must pass and one fails, the clause states the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The rider's claim text cites 14.39 km and $20.64. The fare ledger confirms the charged total is $20.64 and the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is $18.08, a difference of $2.56. But that recomputation only becomes payable where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and here it is not. The rider's arithmetic is not in dispute; its legal premise is.

The driver's counterparty statement is that there was a 'minor detour because of a road works sign.' That assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else under POL-RD-03. The bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02817-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so no advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses and no validity window can be compared. POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's traffic excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

Under POL-RD-13, where the bundle holds no traffic_advisory covering the trip window - status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 - the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and the driver's uncited traffic assertion carries no weight. The driver named no advisory evidence ID, so the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged on that ground.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes. It carries 113 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs fires. The trace is not impaired, so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is to show matching trip identifiers across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown and an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The identifiers match on all three artifacts (TRP-02817), but the excess of 19.92% does not meet the threshold. The rider's initial burden therefore fails at limb (b), and the burden never shifts to the driver.

The fare model is METERED and the payment status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.0. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge in place and the present payment state stands. The rider filed this dispute, so NO_ACTION preserves the $20.64 charge and the driver keeps the fare.

The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 and completed_trips_90d of 174. Under POL-RD-06 the repeat-deviation pattern test requires deviation_flags_90d of 3 or more, or a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 completed trips. Neither limb is met, so no pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. This is the only use to which the driver profile is put, per POL-GEN-01.

The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0. The POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant requires deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more with 1 or fewer substantiated. That condition is not met, so no additional corroboration burden attaches to the rider. I note this against my own side's interest: the rider is not a repeat claimant and the claim was not weakened on that ground.

The chat log for this trip carries zero messages. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or within 3 minutes after, and corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of a waypoint_hint. With no messages at all, no rider-requested detour can be shown, and the driver cannot invoke POL-RD-04 to exonerate any part of the excess. I concede this point against my own side.

The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no amended optimal route exists to re-test the excess against. The booked optimal of 12.0 km stands as the baseline.

The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline is not in play. The 12.0 km booked optimal is the correct baseline for the POL-RD-01 test.

The fare breakdown carries zero ERP gantry lines and zero tolls, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so no airport surcharge line exists. There is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, and POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction has nothing to bite on. No pass-through refund is due to the rider.

The fare breakdown shows distance_charged_km of 14.4 against a trace distance of 14.39 km. The shortfall is 0.01 km, far below the 1.0 km threshold POL-RD-04 sets for DRIVER_COMPENSATION on unbilled distance. No compensation is owed to the driver on that limb, and I do not claim it.

No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. The trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps run backwards or disagree by more than 10 minutes, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing or lacks the required field, the computed refund does not exceed $150.00 or the charged total, and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The case is ripe for a monetary ruling, not an escalation.

ruling.explanation:
Rider: your claim is not supported by the numbers, so the $20.64 charge stands. Driver: no refund and no compensation is due to you, and no conduct referral is made.

THE THRESHOLD DECIDES THE CASE. The trip ran 14.39 km on the trace (EV-GPS-02817, trace_distance_km 14.39; POL-RD-01 says the trace figure governs and the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 14.4 km may not be cited for the test). The booked optimal is 12.0 km (EV-TRIP-02817). Excess = 2.39 km. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be GREATER THAN 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km; both must pass. 2.39 / 12.0 = 19.92%, which is below the 20% gate. The absolute limb passes (2.39 km > 0.8 km) but the proportional limb fails, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome as NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The platform's own derived deviation block records the same result (status 'no deviation'). I note for completeness that even the forbidden rounded figure would give exactly 20.0%, which is likewise not 'greater than 20%'. The rider advocate's first claim (deviation established) is therefore rejected: the trace figure does govern, but it does not clear the 20% limb.

CONSEQUENCES. (a) The POL-RD-02 recomputation does not run, because it applies only 'where a deviation is established'. The rider advocate's arithmetic is itself correct and I record it: recomputed_fare 18.08 = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 16.0) x 1.0 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP, against charged_total 20.64, a difference of 2.56 (payable 2.60 rounded up). That sum only becomes refundable once the POL-RD-01 gate is passed, and it is not, so the rider's claim for it is rejected on its legal premise, not its arithmetic. (b) The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02817) carries no ERP or toll line (erp_lines totals 0.00) and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to bite on and no pass-through or billing-integrity refund is due. Both sides' claims to that effect are accepted. (c) The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (113 fixes, 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, max gap 0.0 s), so no POL-RD-07(a)-(c) limb fires and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; the rider's and driver's clean-trace claims are accepted. (d) No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-02817); no timestamps disagree by more than 10 minutes or run backwards; the computed refund (zero) does not exceed $150.00 or charged_total; and every charge line has a counterpart. The case is ripe for a ruling, not an escalation.

THE DRIVER'S ROAD-WORKS EXPLANATION. The driver's counterparty statement ('Minor detour because of a road works sign') is not needed to decide this case, because no deviation is established.
